suggestions.risk: Store growth and Pages build time; mitigated by committing manifests only, not raw bodies

suggestions.problem: The published standings table disagrees with the official page for 9 of the 12 clubs sampled today because it is a capture dated before the Week 10 Sunday slate, while the results feed already holds those finals.
suggestions.change: Derive the standings table from the results feed at build time and keep the captured table as the dated snapshot it is, with the capture date printed on the row. Add a drift alarm that fails when standings W-L-T disagrees with the replay of the feed.

suggestions.title: Publish the availability blackout window next to any Thursday forecast
suggestions.problem: The official report had not rolled to Week 11 when this session checked (the 2026 selector stops at WEEK 10), so for the Thursday fixture there is at most one published report day before kickoff. A model that silently runs without availability data is not the same product as one that is graded on it.
suggestions.change: Record, per fixture, whether an official report day existed inside the forecast window, and show that flag on the leaderboard row. Do not treat 'no report' as 'no injuries'.
suggestions.how_to_check: Compare the report's week label with the fixture date; the gap is a property of the source calendar, not of our parser.

suggestions.title: Do not carry placeholder scores for fixtures that are already decided
suggestions.problem: The committed feed holds 2026_10_PIT_CIN at status in_progress with scores written as 0-0, while the official page has printed 18-38 FINAL since November 15. Replaying the feed reproduces the official record for 29 of 31 sampled clubs and fails for exactly the two clubs in that fixture.
suggestions.change: Rebuild the feed from a fresh dated capture so that fixture becomes final, and change the writer so a non-final row carries blank scores rather than 0-0 - a numeric placeholder on an open row is read as a result by anything that ignores status. The rebuild belongs to the owning script, so this row asks for it rather than editing the file.
suggestions.how_to_check: Replay the feed's finals against the official records and count the exceptions: it is 2, both from the same fixture, and 0 once that fixture is applied.

suggestions.how_to_check: Count rows in each of the three artefacts and compare with the live official page; the difference is the filter each view applies, which should be printed rather than discovered.

suggestions.title: Make the committed pages regenerable without destroying a hand-added link

suggestions.change: Either move the cross-link into the generator so it is part of the template, or add a CI step that runs the generators and fails on any diff outside the section that owns the file. Do not leave it to memory.
suggestions.how_to_check: Run the generators on a clean tree and diff; today that diff is non-empty, which is the defect.

suggestions.title: Generate clearing numbers from the artefact instead of typing them into the register
suggestions.problem: R27 of the readiness register states the availability-ablation coefficient as a hand-written number, and the derived artefact that the row is supposed to summarise now computes a different one for the same window and the same n. Two pages inside that section therefore publish different betas.
suggestions.change: Have the register's clearing_number be written by the script that computes the ablation, and let the pages read the register - then a re-fit cannot leave a stale sentence behind. Until that happens, every surface quoting this quantity should cite the artefact value and say the register lags.
suggestions.how_to_check: Compare the number in the register row with the number in the derived artefact on every build; the desk does this now and prints the gap when it is non-zero.

suggestions.title: Publish this site as the decision surface, not a dashboard of numbers

suggestions.title: Re-derive the designation-to-play-rate calibration from the league's own archive

suggestions.change: Pull the weekly report per season from nfl.com/injuries/league/{year}/reg{week}, which this session confirmed renders for 2025 and 2024, and re-run the join from the primary source. Keep the mirror numbers as the cross-check rather than the record. This settles the source premise behind R69 and R91; R78 stays partly blocked because the weekly report does not carry inactive lists.
suggestions.how_to_check: Open the two archived pages and count the designation rows; then recompute the rate on one season and compare with the published number.

suggestions.title: Settle the price question with a dated decision, not another inventory

suggestions.change: Choose one of the three options the policy file already lists - buy an archive, self-record dated snapshots of one agreed consensus page, or drop CLV and rank on proper scores only - and record the choice, the date and the owner next to the gate that it unblocks.
suggestions.how_to_check: Count rows with both an open and a close for 2026 in the price store: it is 0, and the readiness register prints the same figure.

suggestions.title: Put the machine-readable copy behind every register page

suggestions.change: Every page table must be generated from a CSV or JSON artefact in the repository; the page links to that artefact in its header. If a table is hand-written, mark it as prose.
suggestions.how_to_check: Count <tr> rows against the source artefact; a page with rows and no artefact fails.

questions.why: Injury
questions.known: Only 2 of 32 official depth charts captured (KC, SEA). nfl.com/teams/{club}/depthchart returns 404 — there is no league-wide official depth endpoint on that path.
questions.missing: Depth for the other 30 clubs; positional criticality weighting.
questions.close: Per-club depth-chart capture, or a licensed roster feed.
questions.priority: No for the framework; yes for the actual scores.

questions.question: Is the NFL spread market efficient enough that a public-data edge exists?
questions.why: Market
questions.known: Secondary literature is split: Levitt (2004) argues books price to maximise profit, not to balance; Boulier et al. (2006) could not reject efficiency; a 10-season home-underdog test found no variation profitable every year.
questions.missing: Whether any inefficiency survives modern limits and vig.
questions.close: Our own backtest on a licensed odds archive.
questions.priority: Yes — this is the single biggest risk to the whole effort.

questions.question: What hold are we actually paying, and does the strategy survive it?
questions.why: Market
questions.known: Computed: -110/-110 implies 52.38% break-even and a 4.76% two-way hold. A 2-leg -110 parlay carries 8.88% effective hold; 6 legs, 24.36%.
questions.missing: Our real average price after line shopping.
questions.close: Bet-level price log.
questions.priority: No — the threshold is known; we just have to clear it.

questions.question: Which prop markets are both available to us and resistant to the league's manipulation concerns?
questions.why: Props
questions.known: The NFL publicly opposes low-engagement, manipulation-prone bets, and states its gambling policy covers prediction markets.
questions.missing: Which specific markets our provider will actually offer at scale.
questions.close: Provider market catalogue.
questions.priority: Yes — scope cannot be set without it.

questions.question: Who is allowed to place a bet, and where?
questions.why: Operations
questions.known: League policy prohibits all NFL personnel from betting on NFL events; players may bet non-NFL events but not from club facilities.
questions.missing: The owner's and any contributor's status. This is a personal legal/eligibility question, not a technical one.
questions.close: Owner confirmation, and local jurisdiction rules.
questions.priority: Yes — build a line-publishing product by default; do not build an auto-bettor until answered.

questions.question: What does 'no manual input' mean when the answer requires a purchasing decision?
questions.why: Operations
questions.known: Nothing in the repo defines budget, vendor approval, or who signs a data contract.
questions.missing: Whether the agent may commit spend. It may not.
questions.close: Owner statement of a spend ceiling and an approved vendor list.
questions.priority: Yes — this is the one hard blocker the agent cannot clear alone.

questions.question: Should the site show live prices, or only originated lines and analysis?
questions.why: Product
questions.known: Undecided; both are buildable.
questions.missing: Depends on Q03 (rights) and Q15 (spend).
questions.close: Answers to Q03 and Q15.

questions.question: Is the deliverable a research artefact, a product, or a betting syndicate?
questions.why: Scope
questions.known: The request mixes all three (leaderboard with rewards, own lines, site).
questions.missing: Which one is primary. Effort splits very differently.
questions.close: Owner prioritisation.
questions.priority: Yes — recommended default: research artefact that publishes lines, not a betting operation.

questions.question: What exactly is the market benchmark we score against
questions.why: Every gate that mentions closing line value needs a price we are allowed to store and publish
questions.known: No usable benchmark for 2026: the mirror carries a closing line for 137 of 148 played games and no timestamp; opening prices exist for 2021 only
questions.close: A dated, hashed capture of one agreed consensus page, twice per week, kept for 4 weeks

questions.question: Do we have the right to store operator prices at all
questions.why: If not, the leaderboard cannot use CLV and must fall back to proper scores alone
questions.known: Unverified. No terms were read for the aggregate mirror; the league page for odds does not exist (nfl.com/odds returns 404)
questions.close: A read of the source terms recorded in docs/SOURCES.md

questions.question: Does an official depth chart exist anywhere in the league
questions.why: Three requirements (register, group slots, stale-row flags) all assume one
questions.known: No. nfl.com has no depth-chart page; club charts are captioned unofficial by the clubs
questions.close: An official artefact that names strings, or a decision to use playing time as the definition

questions.question: Is playing time or listed rank the depth definition
questions.why: It decides whether the backup-deficiency feature can be built at all
questions.known: Recommendation: playing time, because it is measurable and already wrong in the club charts (149 slots carry more than one rank-1 player)
questions.close: Snap-share series per team-position-week from CI

questions.question: How much is a missing starter actually worth
questions.why: A fixed penalty is the single most common modelling error in this space
questions.known: Measured: -0.485 points per expected-miss on the margin, 95% CI [-0.719, -0.251], n=2,367 games (2016-2024). A -3.0 point penalty is far outside the interval
questions.close: Nothing further for the aggregate; per-position coefficients remain unestimated

questions.question: What does Questionable mean on a given field
questions.why: The label is a feature or it is noise depending on the answer
questions.known: Measured on 2016-2024: Questionable plays 64.46% of the time (CI 63.64-65.28, n=13,131); Out 0.02% (n=8,736); Doubtful 0.92% (n=1,522)
questions.close: Nothing; the level may now be replaced by the surprise delta

questions.question: Does 'not listed' mean available
questions.why: No. If it does, the availability feed is complete; if it does not, every absent-but-healthy assumption in earlier work is wrong
questions.known: No. The report mirror carries only Out/Questionable/Probable/Doubtful; a player on reserve is simply absent (0 reserve rows in 42,179)
questions.close: A reserve-list capture per club-week

questions.question: Are parlays priceable from independence at all
questions.why: Ranking a parlay on multiplied marginals is invalid if the legs correlate
questions.known: Same-game side and total legs are near independent in the mirror (phi 0.013, n=2,927) so independence is roughly adequate there; prop legs are unmeasured because no prop prices exist
questions.close: Prop prices plus a joint outcome feed

questions.question: What is our sample until a skill claim is defensible
questions.why: Under-powered leaderboards are the fastest way to publish noise
questions.known: Quantified: at -110 (break-even 52.38%) detecting a 55% bettor at 80% power needs about 2,243 bets; 57% needs 719. On proper scores, 200 graded singles is the escrow floor we chose
questions.close: Nothing; the number is frozen in the pre-registration

questions.question: Which week-10 fixture results are official
questions.why: A feed with a wrong score poisons the ratings for weeks afterward
questions.known: 148 of 150 fixtures reconcile exactly to the official standings on W-L-T and PF/PA (32/32 teams). PIT@CIN and LAC@BAL were not final at capture and are carried blank
questions.close: A later capture of the same schedule page

questions.question: Is the venue in the data the venue that was played
questions.why: Totals, weather and rest all hang off the venue
questions.known: Partly: the mirror carries Melbourne Cricket Ground for the Week 1 international game, so it does track some venues; the Munich fixture is absent from the mirror and the schedule page's own ticketing widget for that fixture names the home club's stadium
questions.close: Per-fixture game-centre capture

questions.question: Do we hold any licensed game-level starter data
questions.why: The brief asks for game books; the site currently has none
questions.known: No. The sample game book carries an explicit media-only copyright notice
questions.close: A licence, or a decision to derive starters from playing time only

questions.question: Where do immutable captures live
questions.why: A static Pages site cannot be the system of record for a growing snapshot history
questions.known: Decided for this section: raw bodies out of the published tree, hashes and counts committed; a real object store still needs the owner
questions.close: An object-store choice and an alert channel

questions.question: Who reconciles six sections into one story
questions.why: Six sections publish the same fixtures at different tiers, which is how a reader gets fooled
questions.known: This section publishes a readiness register keyed to the brief's own requirement list so the reader can see the gate on every line
questions.close: Owner decision on adopting one hub

questions.question: Can we obtain true historical CLOSING lines for spreads, totals and moneylines, and do we know which sportsbook each number came from?
questions.why: Any claim of edge is measured against the price actually available. Without a book-level closing line, a strategy can look profitable against a line no one could bet.

questions.question: Do we have player-prop lines and results at the level needed to test prop strategies?
questions.why: The request covers player prop single bets and prop combinations. Props need historical lines with over/under prices per player per week — a different dataset from team lines.

questions.question: How do we measure how much of the sample the model has effectively already seen?
questions.why: Strategies tuned on 2015-2024 and reported on 2015-2024 are contaminated. The leaderboard is meaningless unless the held-out period is genuinely untouched.

questions.question: What are the empirically measured correlations between legs we intend to combine, and do they hold out of sample?
questions.why: Parlay pricing assumes independence. If legs are positively correlated the true joint probability is higher than the product; the book prices a multiplied edge and we must know the sign and size.

questions.question: Does an official game status actually predict whether a player plays, and by how much, by position and by injury type?
questions.why: The injury signal is the core of the availability model. If 'Questionable' has a stable play rate, it is a usable probability. If it does not, any weighting is invented.

questions.question: When a starter is out, how do we know who replaces him and how large is the drop-off?
questions.why: The request specifically asks to track 2nd/3rd/4th string replacements on defense and offense. Without a defensible replacement map, the downgrade is a guess.

questions.question: What is our own line, and what is the honest baseline it must beat?
questions.why: 'Originating our own lines' only means something relative to the market close. If our line is worse than the close, we have produced noise.

questions.question: What are the legal and licensing constraints on publishing lines, model output and historical odds?
questions.why: Publishing derived lines and redistributing odds can breach vendor terms. The site is public.

questions.question: Can the pipeline run without manual input, and does it fail loudly?
questions.why: The user requires no manual input. Silent data failures would make every downstream number wrong without anyone noticing.

questions.question: What exactly is the sign convention of spread_line, and does the convention match the totals?
questions.why: A sign error silently inverts every cover result and would invalidate every strategy on the site.

questions.question: How do we separate a genuinely skilful strategy from one that is merely a proxy for information already in the line?
questions.why: Many 'edges' are just rediscovering the closing line. The requirement is selectively skill-based strategies, not re-labelled market consensus.

questions.question: Do we have a verified measure of defensive quality by position group, so a backup's impact can be quantified?
questions.why: The request asks for 'deficiencies in defenses'. Deficiencies are relative to a baseline of how well the position group performs.

questions.question: How much of the injury and depth data is missing or contradictory, and how is that represented on the site?
questions.why: The instruction is explicit: if a value cannot be confirmed, leave it blank and flag it. We need a count of how often that happens.

answers.question: Is a multi-season archive of the official weekly injury report reachable at all?
answers.answer: Yes, from the league's own site, at nfl.com/injuries/league/{year}/reg{week}. Two seasons were rendered today (2025 week 10, 2024 week 10) with the practice and game status columns intact.
answers.still_open: Whether the archived page holds the Friday-final version or the last-saved version of that week is not stated on the page; a backtest that needs the exact Wednesday state still has to capture it going forward.

answers.question: Is the Week 10 corpus complete enough to grade the pre-registered baseline?
answers.answer: No. The Monday-night fixture was still live when checked (17-7, Q2), so 148 of 149 games are final. The feed already carries that state instead of guessing.
answers.still_open: Nothing - re-run the capture after the final; this is a timing fact, not a defect.

answers.question: Does an official Week 11 availability report exist before this Thursday's kickoff?
answers.answer: Not yet at the time of checking: the 2026 week selector on the official report stops at WEEK 10, and the page still titles itself as Week 10.
answers.still_open: How many report days will exist before the Thursday fixture - one if the page rolls on Wednesday, zero if it rolls Thursday morning.

answers.question: Is the published standings table consistent with the results feed?
answers.answer: No. 9 of the 12 clubs sampled on the live page disagree with data/standings.json, and every disagreement is one Week 10 game. The replay computed from the feed agrees with the official page, so the feed is sound and the published table is the stale artefact.

answers.question: Can a fixture's venue be taken from the official game centre on demand?
answers.answer: Partly. The game-centre Stadium field was reached for LAC@BAL (M&T Bank Stadium) but the info chunk for IND@HOU could not be fetched twice at the page reader, so that venue stays unverified and the two repository artefacts still disagree (NRG vs Reliant).
answers.still_open: One retry of the game-centre info chunk; until then the value stays blank and flagged.
